terms.definition: A higher-order personality factor identified by Digman. In the Lumina Mandala, it is broadly represented by People Focused, Introversion, Down to Earth and Discipline Driven.
One of the Six Patterns. Qualities that are expressed more strongly in the Everyday Persona than in the Underlying Persona.
A higher-order personality factor identified by Digman. In the Lumina Mandala, it is broadly represented by Inspiration Driven, Big Picture Thinking, Extraversion and Outcome Focused.

A widely researched model of personality based on five broad dimensions: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Neuroticism. It provides the empirical foundation for the Lumina Spark model.
The informal name used for Lumina Spark's Nine Core Purposes: the fundamental reasons for the model's design and application.
Divided into two parts. In the model, each broad Big Five Factor is represented through two contrasting Aspects.
A circular arrangement in which related personality characteristics appear closer together and contrasting characteristics further apart. The Spark Aspects are arranged in this way on the Mandala.
Consideration of the intended and unintended social, ethical and practical consequences of using an assessment.
Evidence that an assessment measures the psychological constructs it is intended to measure.
A statistical measure describing the direction and strength of the relationship between two variables.
A table showing the correlations between multiple variables, allowing the overall pattern of relationships to be examined.
Evidence of how well assessment scores relate to relevant external criteria, such as measures of effective performance.
A reliability coefficient used to examine how consistently the items within a scale work together in measuring the same construct. Sometimes referred to as ‘internal consistency coefficient’.
In factor analysis, instances where a variable is associated with more than one factor rather than loading primarily on its intended factor.
Evidence that different psychological constructs can be distinguished from one another empirically.
The idea that personality contains relatively stable tendencies but can be expressed differently according to context, demands and pressure.
Statistics describing the magnitude of observed differences or relationships, rather than merely whether they are statistically significant.
A Lumina design principle concerned with making personality assessment and development accessible and effective in virtual and digital environments.
A Lumina principle recognising that a person can possess and use apparently opposite personality characteristics rather than having to be one or the other.
The Persona showing how an individual's natural and instinctive tendencies are adapted and managed in everyday working and social life.
A statistical technique used to investigate how variables naturally group together. It is used to examine whether Lumina Qualities group in ways consistent with the intended personality Factors.
A statistical method for examining patterns of relationships between variables and identifying underlying dimensions that help explain them.
Statistics indicating how strongly particular variables or Qualities are associated with an underlying factor.
The overall pattern showing how measured variables relate to underlying factors.
A five-option response scale allowing respondents to indicate the degree to which a questionnaire statement applies to them.
A questionnaire format requiring a respondent to choose between alternatives.
Lumina's high-level colour framework for representing clusters of related personality Qualities in an accessible visual form.
Differences in average scores between gender groups. The manual examines these to investigate whether systematic differences are present in Lumina Quality scores.
One of the Six Patterns. Qualities that are stronger in the Underlying Persona than in the Everyday Persona and may therefore represent natural characteristics that are being tuned down.
An approach emphasising the whole person, individual potential, development and the value of different ways of being rather than reducing people to fixed labels.
The positive, negative or neutral evaluative tone of a questionnaire item.
One of the Six Patterns. Qualities that are strongly present naturally and are also expressed strongly in everyday behaviour.
A response scale allowing respondents to indicate degrees of agreement, endorsement or self-description rather than making a simple either/or choice.
One of the Six Patterns. Qualities that are relatively low in both Underlying and Everyday expression and may take greater effort to use.
The application of the Lumina Spark methodology to recruitment and selection, using norms appropriate to higher-stakes decision making.
The circular visual representation used to show the organisation and relationships of Spark Aspects and Qualities.
A personalised presentation of an individual's Spark results, designed to support interpretation, self-awareness and development.
A visual representation of an individual's personality using blended colours within the Spark Mandala.
A circular visual structure. In Spark, the Mandala displays personality Aspects and Qualities according to their relationships with one another.
The arithmetic average of a set of scores, calculated by adding the scores and dividing by the number of observations.
The middle value when a set of values is arranged in numerical order.
A statistical technique that represents relationships between variables spatially, so variables with more similar relationship patterns tend to appear closer together.
The nine central purposes - or 'Big Whys' - describing why Lumina Spark is designed and applied in the ways set out in the manual.
Nine design aims describing the psychometric principles and intentions underlying the construction of Lumina Spark.
Describes an expression of personality in which an otherwise potentially useful characteristic is taken too far or expressed too strongly for the context.
The Persona illustrating how personality can become exaggerated under sustained pressure, sometimes becoming less effective or less well received.
One of the Six Patterns. Qualities that may sometimes be overplayed or expressed too strongly, particularly under pressure.
One of the Six Patterns. Cases in which opposite Qualities are both strongly present in the same person.
One of three perspectives through which a Lumina Quality is explored: Underlying, Everyday and Overextended.
Collectively, the Underlying, Everyday and Overextended perspectives used to show different forms of personality expression.
Evidence concerning how effectively assessment scores can predict a relevant outcome, such as aspects of future performance.
Relating to the scientific measurement of psychological characteristics such as personality.
The field concerned with the theory and methods used to measure psychological characteristics and evaluate the quality of those measurements.
The degree to which an assessment produces consistent and sufficiently stable measurements.
Analysis of the positive, neutral or negative tone of language. The manual uses it to investigate the evaluative wording of questionnaire items.
The amount of variation that different variables or questionnaire items have in common.
Six ways of interpreting combinations of Spark scores: Key Qualities, Hidden Treasures, Amplifications, Low Qualities, Overextensions and Paradoxes.
Lumina's term for the detailed psychometric information underlying the model, designed to be translated into accessible and practically useful insights.
The tendency for people to give answers they believe will be viewed favourably rather than answering solely according to their actual characteristics.
A statistic describing how widely scores are spread around their mean. A larger standard deviation indicates greater variability in the scores.

Describes a result that meets a specified statistical threshold indicating that the observed difference or relationship would be relatively unlikely under the relevant null hypothesis. It does not by itself indicate that the effect is large or important.
The degree to which measurement properties or scores remain consistent over time.
Evidence of reliability obtained by comparing scores from the same people across two assessment occasions. Strong correlations between occasions indicate greater stability.
The Underlying, Everyday and Overextended Personas through which each Lumina Quality is explored.
A relatively enduring personality characteristic on which individuals can differ by degree.
An approach to personality that describes people in terms of continuous characteristics rather than assigning them to discrete personality types.
A central Lumina principle: personality is measured as a set of continuous traits rather than by placing individuals into fixed categories.
An optimisation algorithm that searches for a short route through a set of locations. The manual uses it to explore a route through the MDS-derived positions of the Spark Qualities.
The visual route produced through the MDS arrangement of the 24 Spark Qualities, used to compare the correlation-derived organisation with the familiar Spark Mandala.
The Persona reflecting an individual's natural and instinctive tendencies when situational demands are relatively low.
The extent to which an assessment is perceived as valid, relevant and useful by practitioners and the people who use it.
The sentiment-analysis method used in the manual to classify questionnaire wording as positive, neutral or negative.
The extent to which evidence supports the interpretation that an assessment measures what it is intended to measure and that appropriate conclusions can be drawn from its scores.
A statistical measure of the amount of variation among a set of scores.
